confidence_notes: I checked food and drink prices with four web searches: one for the RBA rate and three covering San Antonio prices. For coffee, the inexpensive meal, the mid-range meal for two and beer, I used cost-of-living aggregators. The most recent was Expatica's Numbeo-based figures from June 2026: cappuccino about $5.19, inexpensive meal $18, three-course meal for two $65 and domestic draft beer $5.25. Other sources gave higher figures, such as LivingCost at $6.15 for a 0.5 L pub beer and Expatistan at about $8. Some of those sources are older or have no date. For the July 2026 window I rounded slightly upward and adjusted for tourist-area prices. The cocktail estimate is less certain. Square's bar price data, which has no date, gave averages of about $8-10, while individual bar menus showed $12-15, so I chose a middle value. Wine is the least certain drink price. I found no citywide average, only single-venue menus showing roughly $8-12 for a casual glass and $15 or more at upscale places. I set it a little above beer, matching the local price relationship. All four accommodation prices are my own estimates from general knowledge, not from searches or listings. San Antonio has very few registered hostels, so the hostel dorm and private-room prices are especially uncertain. July is hot and is not peak season, though River Walk and downtown hotels cost more.
comparable_city_reasoning: I treated San Antonio as a lower-cost large city in Texas and the US Sun Belt, priced similarly to Houston and Dallas and generally cheaper than Austin. I benchmarked accommodation against typical rates for budget motels and mid-range chain hotels in mid-tier US tourist cities.
